mohan: kicking off canary for nova-lite-int4 on canary-2. seeing funcall JSON parse failures when batch size > 1 and kvcache is warm. small reproducible spike in parse errors, ~6-8% of calls. :eyes:

lina: same here, reproduced locally with microbatch=2. pasted one of the raw completions below — it ends with a half-closed array and some trailing tokens. not a simple punctuation slip.

lina: ```
{
  "tool": "get_weather",
  "args": {
    "city": "seattle",
    "units": "metric"
  },
  "metadata": [
    {"source": "user_profile"},

  
```

aya: looks like the model emits an extra newline and then a partial token that confuses the JSON parser. happens more once kv cache has a long prefix. maybe kvcache chunking / k/v boundary influences generation boundary.

sam: quick thought — is sampling/nonzero temp on canary? non-determinism + batching could produce truncated suffixes. can we run with temp=0 for a trial?

mohan: canary config currently has temp=0.2 for this run to simulate prod. also have continuous batching enabled. ci-bot reported: 

ci-bot: Canary job #403: parse_error_rate=0.067, threshold=0.02 -> FAILED canary check. logs at /canaries/403/trace.txt

sam: ok. heuristic rescue might be lower-risk than flipping production sampling. propose two parallel experiments: (A) disable continuous batching for nova-lite-int4 canary, (B) keep batching but enable "soft-parse-rescue" runtime toggle that attempts a minimal fixup before giving up.

aya: for soft-parse-rescue ideas: 1) trim trailing whitespace + incomplete escape sequences, 2) try to balance braces by appending up to 8 closing brackets/braces, 3) attempt ndjson wrap if top-level array/object ambiguous. will add a smoke parser.

sam: example repair helper I used: 
```python
def quick_repair(s):
    # strip trailing ANSI/newline noise
    s = s.rstrip('\\n\\r ')
    # try balance braces
    for _ in range(8):
        try:
            return json.loads(s)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            # heuristically append closing braces/brackets
            s += '}'
    # fallback: try ndjson split
    parts = s.split('\\n')
    for p in parts[::-1]:
        try:
            return json.loads(p)
        except:
            continue
    raise
```

lina: that's reasonable as a canary-only mitigation. we should emit telemetry flags so we can tell which repairs succeeded vs which calls truly returned valid json originally. add a header on the trace: `x-parse-repair: attempted|none|succeeded`

mohan: agreed. also concerned about semantic regressions if repair masks upstream model hallucinations (e.g., repaired text could be wrong tool args). we need a metric: repaired_calls_with_tool_mismatch. will add a small eval that replays repaired outputs through strict-schema-check to see if semantics changed.

aya: another debug angle: capture the last 128 tokens of the model with raw token ids and detokenized text plus the kvcache slice boundaries. that helped earlier when we diagnosed kvprefix truncation issues.

sam: low-effort rollout plan: 1) create two canaries (batch-off + soft-repair-on), 2) add telemetry to tag repaired outputs and emit last-128 tokens, 3) run for 12h, compare parse_error_rate, repair_success_rate, semantic_mismatch_rate. deadline: EOD tomorrow for initial samples.

mohan: created INF-3427 for tracking, linking canaries and the evaluation notebook. I'll run the batch-off canary first, then the soft-rescue one. will post results here. thanks. :thumbsup:
